title: Recall Quiz: Early Romantics: Blake & Wordsworth

questions.q: The publication of which book in 1798 is generally considered the beginning of the Romantic movement in England?
questions.explanation: Lyrical Ballads by Wordsworth and Coleridge marked a radical shift in poetry.

questions.q: Who defined poetry as 'the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings'?
questions.explanation: Wordsworth wrote this in his famous Preface to the Lyrical Ballads.

questions.q: Which of William Blake's poetry collections contains the famous poem 'The Tyger'?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
questions.explanation: 'The Tyger' is the dark counterpart to 'The Lamb' from Songs of Innocence.

questions.q: William Wordsworth's massive autobiographical epic poem, which traces the growth of his poetical mind, is titled:
questions.explanation: The Prelude was published posthumously in 1850.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a core characteristic of Romanticism?
options: Strict adherence to classical literary rules
Celebration of the individual and emotion
Interest in the supernatural and mystical
questions.explanation: Romanticism was a rebellion *against* the strict classical rules of the previous age.

questions.q: The famous line 'The Child is father of the Man' was written by:
questions.explanation: This line from 'My Heart Leaps Up' encapsulates Wordsworth's belief in the purity and importance of childhood.

questions.q: Which poet is best known for his 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'?
questions.explanation: Thomas Gray is the most famous of the Graveyard Poets or Pre-Romantics.

questions.q: Which of the following poets collaborated with William Wordsworth to produce 'Lyrical Ballads'?
questions.explanation: Coleridge provided four poems for the collection, including The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
